figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 1.   Reactions catalyzed by BBE-­like enzymes. (A) Typical oxidative dehydrogenation and oxidative cyclization reactions catalyzed by BBE-­like enzymes from 
plants. (B) BBE-­like enzymes from Moraceae plants in the biosynthesis pathway of D-­A type natural products. BBE-­like oxidocyclases from Morus alba (MaOCs) 
catalyze oxidative cyclization of moracin C (1) to yield benzopyran-­type natural product moracin D (2) while the BBE-­like diene synthases (MaDSs) catalyze the 
oxidative dehydrogenation of moracin C (1) to yield diene 3, which further undergoes an enzymatic intermolecular Diels–Alder (D-­A) reaction with morachalcone 
A (4) to yield the D-­A type natural product chalcomoracin (5) in the presence of BBE-­like Diels–Alderases (MaDAs).

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 2.   Crystal structure of MaDS1 and structure-­based mutagenesis studies. (A) The overall structure of MaDS1 is shown in a ribbon model. α-­helices, cyan; β-­
strands, magenta; loops, light pink. The FAD cofactor (yellow and shown in a stick representation) forms two covalent bonds with MaDS1, as shown in the 2Fo−Fc 
electron density map (blue mesh, contoured at the 1.0σ level) for FAD and the covalently bound His114 and Cys176 (blue and shown in stick representation). (B) 
Topology structure of MaDS1. α-­helices, cyan; β-­strands, magenta. (C) Superposition of docked model of moracin C and compound 14 observed in the cocrystal 
structure (PDB: 8ZLT). The FAD cofactor (yellow and shown in a stick representation) forms 2 covalent bonds with MaDS1, as shown in the 2Fo−Fc electron 
density map (blue mesh, contoured at the 1.0σ level) for FAD and the covalently bound H114 and C176 (white and shown in stick representation). The ligand 
compound 14 (green, shown in a stick representation) fits into the predicted substrate binding pocket, as shown in the 2Fo−Fc electron density map (blue mesh, 
contoured at the 1.0σ level). The docked model of MaDS1 with moracin C (cyan) superposed with the cocrystal structure. The FAD cofactor, D175, and substrate 
(shown in stick representation) overlap in the two models. The distance between D175 and the prenyl group is 3.3 Å in the docking model (red dotted lines) and 
3.6 Å in the cocrystal structure (purple dotted lines). The H atom of the benzylic carbon of the substrate is closely located to the FAD (2.8 Å), as indicated by the 
green dotted line in the docking model and the blue dotted line in the cocrystal structure. (D) The binding mode of moracin C (1) in MaDS1. Stereo views of the 
docking model show the interactions between 1 (green) and nearby residues (yellow). FAD is depicted in gray, and hydrogen-­bonding interactions are illustrated 
as yellow dotted lines. The distance between D175 and the prenyl group is 3.6 Å (indicated by the red dotted lines). The H atom of the benzylic carbon of the 
substrate is closely located to the FAD (2.8 Å), as indicated by the blue dotted line. (E) The relative enzymatic activities of MaDS1 variants. Enzymatic reactions 
were performed with 0.3 μg purified MaDS1 variants and 100 μM of 1 in a 20 mM Tris-­HCl solution at pH 8.0 and 50 °C for 7 min. Relative oxidative cyclization 
(blue) and dehydrogenation (red) activities of MaDS1 variants. “ND” signifies not detected. The data are presented as mean values ± SE, with error bars indicating 
the SD of three independent replications.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 3.   Identification of critical residues for the oxidative dehydrogenation reaction. (A) Sequence logos illustrate the 4 important residues for the enzymatic 
activity. (B) UPLC analysis of the oxidative activity of MaDS1 and D175 variants with 1 as substrate. Enzymatic reactions were performed with 3 mg purified MaDS1 
and variant and 100 μM of 1 in a 10 mM Tris-­HCl solution at pH 8.0 and 50 °C for 0.5 h. Relative oxidative cyclization (blue) and dehydrogenation (red) activities of 
MaDS1 variants. “ND” signifies not detected. The data are presented as mean values ± SE, with error bars indicating the SD of three independent replications. (C) 
UPLC analysis of the oxidative activity of variants of other oxidases from Morus alba. Enzymatic reactions of MaMO, MaDS5, and their mutants were performed 
using 5 mg of purified enzymes and variants, along with 100 μM of 1, in a 10 mM Tris-­HCl solution at pH 8.0 and 50 °C for 30 min. Enzymatic reactions of ancDADS 
and mutants were performed with 1 mg of purified enzymes and variants and 100 μM of 1 in a 10 mM Tris-­HCl solution at pH 8.0 and 50 °C for 30 min.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Fig. 4.   The Gibbs free energy (in kcal/mol) profile for the oxidative cyclization of moracin C catalyzed by MaDS1 with critical intermediates and transition states. 
All energetics were calculated at the level of M062X/6-­311++G(d,p), SMD (Water)//B3LYP-­D3/6-­31G(d), SMD (Water). The red pathway follows a deprotonation-­
oxidation sequence. The black pathway follows an oxidation-­deprotonation-­6π electrocyclization sequence (without enzyme). The orange pathway proceeds 
via oxidation followed by deprotonation to yield alkene products. The dashed line pathway represents the 6π electrocyclization that occurs within the enzyme.

Fig. 5.   Theozyme calculations of M-­TS4, M-­TS5, M-­TS6, and their variants. (A) Comparison of three selectivity-­determining step transition states of the nonmutated 
enzyme. (B) Comparison of three selectivity-­determining step transition states after D175 mutation to carboxylic acid. (C) Comparison of three selectivity-­
